One complete rational source certificate reports a finite upper-bound improvement at the exact side it states: s(261) <= .
All three retained jobs, the positive with its duplicate-square and outside-container controls, were decided again here on 14 October 2026 by both maintained exact routes and equal their retained rows. A third exact route, half-extent containment and exact intersection area, decided the certificate with six controls each and held the derived fact to the pinned file it is derived from, fetched at the pin. No route here is the source's code; the source's runs of this repository's two maintained routes on its corners witnesses are its own and decide nothing here, so the replay is independently re-implemented. Those statements are the author's; no source program ran here.

Measured pose by pose by that review, it is Robert Barnett's packing (T-150) re-solved, no square moved beyond 2e-06; squares touch the box and the closest pair touches, which the closed box allows. claim.base:
PingYou Ltd's pull request 574 reports finite upper-bound improvements at 68 counts: sixty-four complete rational source certificates, at 68, 84, 86, 88, 102, 103, 105, 108, 110, 123, 126, 127, 129, 130, 131, 132, 146, 155, 156, 172, 175, 176, 179, 180, 181, 182, 199, 204, 206, 208, 209, 210, 211, 228, 232, 236, 237, 238, 239, 240, 241, 258, 259, 261, 263, 264, 266, 267, 268, 269, 270, 271, 272, 273, 292, 295, 297, 301, 303, 304, 305, 306, 307 and 308, and algebraic ones at 70, 153, 207 and 302. Each rational side is a fraction whose numerator runs to 92 to 1,787 digits; the packet's claims record (acquisition/claims.json in pingyou-pr574-certificates-2026-10-13) states each exactly, and the notes compare each with its case and the earlier reports.
Its algebraic supplement states s(70) <= 8.880960371555579594696691574923…, s(153) <= 12.870013850404464344460153400780…, s(207) <= 14.880960371555579594696691574923… and s(302) <= 17.870275382555059669572692573398…, roots of integer polynomials of degree 5, 7, 5 and 3, as exact witnesses over their fields.
The author reports that a standard-library exact checker of its own, by separating axes and by rational polygon clipping, accepts all 147 v2 certificates and their pre-batch comparators with 2,678,449 unordered pairs per checker, rejects duplicate-square and outside-container controls, and that this repository's packing-witness verify and check_rational_witness_independent, run unchanged, accept every native corners Witness/v2 of the v2 release; and, for the supplement, that its checker isolates each declared real root by rational Sturm counts and accepts the 60 exact certificates with 917,302 pairs, and that the native verifier accepts their native witnesses. Those statements are the author's; no source program ran here.
Here both maintained exact routes decided all 64 rational certificates with their two controls each, and sqpack's exact witness verifier decided the four algebraic ones over their fields; no second route over a number field exists here. The third exact route decided the 64 rational certificates again with six controls each, and no route here is the source's code; the source's runs of this repository's two maintained routes are its own and decide nothing here, so the replay is independently re-implemented. The 14 October review of the pull request found no blocking defect.
Credit PingYou Ltd (https://github.com/BuddenPing/square-packing-certificates) with the certificate refinements, as the submission asks: smaller padding, an exact common-centre crop or an exact re-solve of each packing's own contacts. The packings are others': the submission names per count the original construction authors and preceding refiners it starts from, among them Erich Friedman's and David Ellsworth's catalogue constructions as Evan Daniel's exact certificates and regularized lists state them, Ryan Xu, Robert Barnett, Francisco Couzo, Daniil Ostashev, Nate Chaoweeraprasit (SQUISH), Siddharth Gupta, Kevin Fang and Mykhailo Polkovskyi (Mishapolk), and it says that padding reduction does not transfer authorship of an existing packing.
The pull request names at each count but 176 the registered packing whose certificate it tightens; at 176 it states Daniil Ostashev's packing of issue 575, which the record registers at no count there, every square within 9.6e-13 of his and the side 1.4e-19 below his certificate. Measured pose by pose by the 14 October review, the certificate is the named packing with no square moved beyond 1e-03 at 27 of those counts, pairs with it one to one with squares moved beyond 1e-03 at 33, and at 199, 292 and 303 pairs with it, or with any registered packing there, nowhere one to one; each count's regularizations item records which. At 199 the poses are those issue 593 states later.
The source makes no statement about AI assistance in this pull request; for its #503 and #504 certificates the author said on 12 October 2026 that they were AI assisted by 'PY', an unreleased agentic AI offering by PingYou Ltd.
The per-count ledger of 14 October (jlevy/squares#601) records it at these 68 counts, each below every earlier report there, and at no other: at 59 counts it ties or trails an earlier report, and at 21 the printed precision did not decide it.
Seventeen of those 21 are now decided exactly, by devtools.decide_undecided_comparisons. At 14 counts the pull request's side is above the standing one: the case records' reported lanes at 17, 28, 37, 39, 41, 69, 87, 128, 205, 235 and 300, and the entries pending adoption at 106, 152 and 177, T-121, T-122 and T-123. At 54, 107 and 178 it equals the reported lane. It is recorded at none of the 17. At 29, 55, 71 and 83 the comparison stays undecided, because the record holds only a print of the standing side.
The 14 October review recommends this entry as the house at the 60 rational counts where it was then the smallest exact side. On 15 October 2026 the coordinator of the 14 October intake held those houses for the owner (devtools.select_houses.LIFTED keeps the hold's words): their witnesses would add about 18.5 MB to a checkout and their custody inputs about 5.8 MB to every worker's snapshot. The owner's house rule of 16 October 2026 lifted the hold: size is met by OR-18's means, never by holding a house, and the houses are staged for adoption (devtools.select_houses.PENDING_ADOPTION).
The hold skipped this entry only: at 105, 129, 146, 156, 176, 204, 261, 271, 272 and 303 the next certificate below the case that a replay here decided and a review accepted held it from that day (T-170, T-162, T-168, T-161, T-165, T-162, T-169, T-161, T-171, T-162), this entry being smaller by 1.7e-99 to 1.18e-02, and at the other 50 counts the cases kept their houses. The adoption of 16 October 2026 (PR #657) then took ten of the 60 below this entry, 146 to T-187 and 129, 156, 175, 176, 204, 232, 264, 271 and 303 to T-186. The other 50 move to this entry when the staged adoption lands, under think-3mry.
At 70, 153 and 207 the algebraic certificates are the smallest sides known but rest on one route; the rule of 15 October left them out for the owner (RP-3), and the house rule of 16 October 2026 adopts them, staged under think-ot5c until the writer takes an algebraic side; meanwhile the case at 70 keeps its house and Mykhailo Polkovskyi's issue 573 (T-173) holds 153 and 207. At 211, 237, 241, 302 and 304 smaller certificates hold the cases (T-188, T-190, T-182, T-186, T-186).

significance.rationale: Tighter certificates of packings the record credits to others, by padding or an exact re-solve, 1e-99 to 1e-19 below the case ceilings at most counts, as T-155; the 1.70e-02 drop below the case at 176 belongs to Daniil Ostashev's packing of issue 575; a citable detail of each case that moves no theorem; no lower bound or optimum.

reviews.scope: Finite feasibility of PR 574's 64 rational and four algebraic certificates: the frozen claim records rebuilt, the 64 rational receipts admitted after the import lane's two complete replays, the four algebraic counts' 12 jobs decided again on their one route, the 64 rational certificates decided by the third exact route with its sharp controls, every pinned file and the four release assets fetched and held to their sizes and digests, each rational fact read again from its release-asset member, and each count measured pose by pose against the packing its regularizations item names.
